messages:
anya: Quick thread - I ran a cross-accelerator sweep on batch-cap sensitivity (A10 / T4 / L4 / A100 / H100). Observed unexpected perf cliffing and KV-cache fragmentation when max_tokens_per_batch goes above certain values. Sharing short notes + raw sample below.

mike: Thanks. Which workload and model? throughput or p50 latency target?

anya: Running convo-chat-8k-ish traces (avg len ~420 tokens) with gpt-style decoder on quantized weights. Targets: p50 <= 120ms for interactive tier, throughput for background qps bench.

anya: Quick raw run command we used:
```
./run_inference_bench --model redwood-chat-8k-q8 --gpu A100 --concurrency 16 --max_tokens_per_batch=65536 --kv_cache=true --batching=continuous --warmup=200
```

anya: Results snippet (median of 3 runs):
- A10 @ max_tokens_per_batch=65536 -> p50 115ms, 95th 290ms, observed kernel fallback on later steps, throughput drop ~22% after 60s.
- T4 @ 32768 -> p50 210ms, 95th 450ms, steady but high latency.
- L4 @ 49152 -> p50 135ms, 95th 320ms, occasional KV-cache churn leading to 20% throughput jitter.
- A100 @ 131072 -> p50 90ms, 95th 210ms, stable.
- H100 @ 98304 -> p50 100ms initially, then 95th spikes to 520ms after ~30s, memory compaction churn noted.

derek: The H100 symptoms sound like a kernel selection oscillation combined with KV allocation fragmentation. We recently changed the fallback kernel order in kernel-selector (PR #4126) which causes large-batch paths to pick a different GEMM kernel for >64k tokens. That kernel has worse per-step latency in the streaming case (higher setup cost) but wins at huge batched matmuls. With continuous batching we flip between small and huge aggregates -> thrashing.

olivia: Interesting — L4's jitter aligns with our earlier observation that L4 warms into a different attention kernel at larger sequence-window. For L4 the per-request token distribution has a heavier tail in this trace, so continuous batching pushes it over the threshold sometimes.

neha: FYI I noticed a perf regression in last week's runtime merge (commit d8f3b2) that adjusted the KV allocator to prefer smaller free chunks. That reduces worst-case single-allocation latency but increases fragmentation for long-lived KV usage. Might be compounding the H100 issue.

anya: TL;DR initial hypotheses: (1) kernel-selector policy + continuous batching causes oscillation for certain token budgets, (2) KV allocator fragmentation exacerbates H100 long-run spikes, (3) optimal max_tokens_per_batch is hardware-dependent and non-monotonic.

mike: Can you propose per-GPU initial caps so we can A/B in staging? I can run 12-hour soak tests.

anya: Proposed conservative defaults (to test):
- T4: max_tokens_per_batch = 32768 (keep low to avoid large matmul slow path)
- L4: max_tokens_per_batch = 49152 (L4 prefers intermediate caps to avoid kernel flip)
- A10: max_tokens_per_batch = 65536 (A10 memory / kernel mix seems okay)
- H100: max_tokens_per_batch = 98304 (but also enforce kv_compaction_threshold => 0.6)
- A100: max_tokens_per_batch = 131072 (stable in our runs)

olivia: For H100 I'd rather test two configs: 98k with current allocator, and 80k with a small allocator tweak (prefer larger free chunks). That will isolate KV fragmentation effect.

neha: I can open a small runtime PR to add a feature flag: `runtime.kv_allocator.prefer_large_free_chunks` (default false). Will attach microbenchmarks.

derek: Also propose smoothing kernel-selector thresholds: add hysteresis so we don't flip kernel selection on transient batch spikes. Simple approach: require > N consecutive aggregated steps above token_threshold before switching kernel. N=3?

anya: Agreed. My plan: 1) run the A/B caps for each GPU + hysteresis knobs, 2) run allocator toggle on H100, 3) collect p50/p95, throughput, and KV free-list histogram every 5m. Test plan in /experiments/batch-cap-sensitivity (will PR).

mike: I'll run soak jobs starting tomorrow on staging (reserved pools). Schedule: 12h per config, gather metrics with trace_id `cross-accel-2287654321`.

olivia: I'll add the hysteresis change as a small opt-in flag behind `runtime.kernel_selector.hysteresis_steps` default 0 for now.
